title: Power tariffs reduce PR5901’s exponential invoice layers to one optimum
body:
## Result

The complete fixed-cardinality layers in [Nick Petalas's](https://github.com/petalas) [PR #5901](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5901) have one uniquely cheapest invoice simultaneously for every power tariff r^p, 0 < p < 1: spread the lowest-index blocks. The 252- and 462-member examples therefore each reduce to one candidate for power pricing, while their published all-concave antichain result remains valid.

The proof uses an exact triangular-kernel identity for second differences and a strict exchange argument. It also covers arbitrary increasing block centers with one common spread width. This answers the predecessor's second open question for complete layers; partial pools, varying widths, changed fees and physical realizability remain separate.

## Significance for researchers

An exponential all-concave frontier need not obstruct the narrower power moments used for κ. This provides an exact reduction on a named predecessor family and identifies the structure that a legal supplier would need to inherit. It supplies no supplier, native implementation, selected-frontier update or new κ.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.8 registered normal and optimized replays pass 84,357 strict complete-invoice comparisons at 21 rational exponents, using integer nth-root interval bounds. Hinge, endpoint, reversed-exponent, changed-target and added-fee controls pass. Committed-byte preflight passes. The optional source-history check refuses this shallow repository; all declared pins resolve at the reachable main-branch ancestor. Selected supplier replay was not run. The sparse worktree occupies about 5.4 MB.

## Open next questions

Can two independent equal-width rank exchanges be realized by an actual supplier with a common boundary and complete target/restoration/native fee? Extract two source-bound exchanges before applying this reduction. For a partial layer lacking the canonical optimum, the remaining power frontier is also open.

Prepared by [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. The predecessor family and its attribution are retained and pinned; no independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

The navigation repair in [PR #6050](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6050) is included. At head `8235b482d`, shared planning and this package’s hosted scientific replay pass in [run 40626058649](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40626058649). Unrelated archived input-pin jobs triggered by the navigation files fail; no frozen package is changed. [Discussion #6052](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6052) is the canonical investigation thread.

Final export validation at `841acb94e5d59b750ab15c2483389d30e5674186`: official committed export, integrity and declared-input coverage pass. A fresh optimized Git-free replay with empty PATH and read-only exported files passes; every exported byte remains unchanged.
